failedCheck.description: A run of the batch that did not pass, as the runner filed it.

check.description: The dev.knotless.check record of the run, with its steps and log.

status.description: How it ended, as dev.knotless.check's status says.

workflow.description: The workflow's name, as its file in .knotless/workflows names it.

main.description: Kept in the account of whoever wrote it; for a private repository, in their repo inside the repository's space. Readers take the latest about a pull from the repository's owner or a collaborator, who may merge it, and from no one else. A pull is in the queue while that is `queued` and the pull is open, in the order of those records' keys. A runner the repository names takes queued pulls in that order, a few at a time, squashes each onto the branch as a commit of its own, runs the workflows that run on a pull into the branch once, at the last of them, and once those pass moves the branch there, marking each pull `merged` with a dev.knotless.state. One that does not apply, or that its checks find breaks the branch, it marks `ejected`.

checks.description: For `ejected` by a batch that failed its checks, those that did not pass.

commit.description: The hex object ID of the pull's head: for `queued`, the one queued; for `ejected`, the one turned away.

reason.description: For `ejected`, why: the paths it conflicts in, or the checks that failed and where to read their logs.

repo.description: The repository the pull is on.

state.description: `queued` puts the pull at the back of the queue; `left` takes it out; `ejected` is the runner turning it away, saying why in `reason`.

subject.description: The dev.knotless.pull queued, taken out or turned away.

description: A pull put in the merge queue of the branch it targets, taken out of it, or turned away by the runner that lands the queue.
